lens: Does the first frame after every attack press show a big pose clearly different from standby?
look_for: An instant jump into the windup; charge moves holding and shaking; light moves out almost immediately.
red_flags: Ease-outs from idle; first frames you can't tell apart from standby; 'the controls feel delayed' on a lag-free display.

lens: Pause on each attack's contact frame: is it the strongest, clearest pose, and does the hitbox sit on it?
look_for: Strong, twisted, readable hit poses; collision starting once the swing is strong; visuals and hitboxes that agree.
red_flags: Half-formed poses frozen by hit stop; hits that look like they connect but don't; swings that keep hitting after they end.

lens: From the farthest gameplay camera, can you read every attack and every hit reaction at a glance?
look_for: Exaggerated poses, extreme damage frames unlike standby, faces pushed past 'done', review done at real size.
red_flags: Animations approved only in close-up; damage poses near standby; subtle faces on tiny characters.

lens: Does the follow-through show what just happened and how heavy it was, and look nothing like standby?
look_for: Big, momentum-carrying recoveries on their own path, held until cancel frames, full landings.
red_flags: Interpolating straight back to idle; recoveries that fizzle; reverse playback of the attack.

lens: Is any motion mushy from interpolation or long blends, or too fast to register?
look_for: Key poses arriving quickly, short blends, secondary motion with enough frames to read.
red_flags: Moves that feel slow despite low frame counts; distorted blends; wings or cloth snapping in two frames.

lens: Does anything move like a machine: single-axis turns, center pivots, straight-line flight, straight wrists?
look_for: Two-axis turns, linked joints, off-center pivots, wobble and recoil, hand-tuned curves.
red_flags: Robotic head turns, drill-like wrists, perfectly centered spins, default function curves.

lens: Filled in black, from the gameplay camera, on both sides of the screen, is every key pose readable and asymmetric?
look_for: All four limbs visible in profile, twists instead of side bends, faces visible from both sides.
red_flags: Symmetric poses, flat sideways knockback, characters facing away on one side.

lens: Has every move been checked in all its versions: ground and air, each direction, each facing and each target stance?
look_for: Side-by-side variant reviews, reach tests in all directions, combo tests against every reaction stance.
red_flags: Aerial versions with different poses; reach that shrinks in one direction; combos that drop on some stances.

lens: Rank every sound by relevance to the player: is the loudest sound always the most important one?
look_for: A written priority ladder; decisive events and hits on top; voices balanced; ambience lowest.
red_flags: Volumes set by action size; ambience or chatter masking hits; everything equally loud.

lens: In the worst-case scene (most players, most effects), can you hear exactly when each hit starts?
look_for: Short attacks, short tails, jabs pared down, heavy hits finished inside hitstop.
red_flags: A sea of noise; hit sounds that swell in late or ring over the next hit.

lens: Does the mix still work on a cheap TV, and has the playback chain been checked for lag?
look_for: Approval on headphones, PC speakers and a cheap TV; punch that survives without bass; fixed reference gear; latency checked.
red_flags: Studio-only sign-off; impacts that vanish on TV speakers; changed headphones mid-project.

lens: Stop anywhere and listen: is there dead silence, or ambience burying something important?
look_for: Quiet, fairly realistic layers everywhere; a soundscape matched to the visuals.
red_flags: Silence when action stops; busy ambience over key effects; music that sticks out over detailed visuals.

lens: With the sound off, can a player still see every warning, and does sound carry what it should for those who rely on it?
look_for: A visual tell for every audio warning; optional audio and vibration cues.
red_flags: Attacks signaled only by sound; information only in voice lines.

lens: Can players hum the main theme, and does each scene's tempo and mood fit its action and feeling?
look_for: A main theme with arrangements; BPM targets per scene; music structured around countdowns, match length and climaxes.
red_flags: Too many forgettable songs; one tempo everywhere; loops that restart mid-match.

lens: For each sound, is its job impact or information, and does its realism fit both the job and the visuals?
look_for: Exaggerated hits, realistic materials and ambience, footsteps that ground characters.
red_flags: Slappy realistic punches; cartoon effects over photoreal art; hovering characters with silent feet.

lens: Could the sound designer or composer act on your request alone, and are you judging their work by fit rather than by your mental image?
look_for: Concrete roles, known comparisons, links, references with keep/drop notes; approvals based on fit.
red_flags: 'More clang'; 'make it like this'; rejecting fitting work for being different.

lens: Who is the target player, and what does a "minor" risk feel like to them?
look_for: A written target by experience level and risk dials set to match it.
red_flags: Difficulty tuned to the team; one-hit deaths or heavy inertia in a game for newcomers.

lens: Can a player using only the simplest core finish the game or hold their own?
look_for: A core-only playthrough that works; depth that is optional; hard inputs rewarded but not required.
red_flags: Progress or competitiveness gated on the depth system or on hard inputs.

lens: What happens to a player who fails the same spot ten times?
look_for: Difficulty changeable anytime, an offer to ease off or skip without shame, variety on the way back.
red_flags: A forced restart, an impossible spike, the same scenery every attempt.

lens: How many seconds pass between 'Ugh, I blew it!' and the next input?
look_for: About a second of punchy failure feedback, then control, at a safe respawn.
red_flags: Long fades, loads, unskippable text, respawning into enemy fire.

lens: Who set this difficulty, and how well do they know the game?
look_for: Tuning done handicapped, then lowered again; fresh testers used once each.
red_flags: 'The best player on the team can just about clear it.'

lens: After this balance change, does every option still have a peak and a valley?
look_for: Distinct strengths and weaknesses; fixes made to secondary parameters; win rates in a narrow band; options that still feel different.
red_flags: Options converging; signature strengths shaved; weaknesses patched in the same change.

lens: Could a player lose purely because of luck?
look_for: Random events players can respond to; randomness that rewards skill or enables comebacks in casual modes.
red_flags: Single rolls deciding outcomes in skill contests; manipulable random numbers.

lens: Does each penalty match how bad the mistake was, and is there a way back?
look_for: Small slips cost little, big blunders cost more, every irreversible choice has a recovery path.
red_flags: Instant death for a missed jump; all power-ups wiped; permanent penalties with no redemption.

lens: How much does this game help the player who is behind, and was that a decision?
look_for: A stated choice between casual catch-up and skill-reflecting chaos, plus handicap options for mismatched groups.
red_flags: The same player winning every casual match, or stat buffs for losers in a skill game.

lens: Where are the peaks and flats on your difficulty curve?
look_for: Bosses as peaks with rewards, breathers and farming spots as flats, no late impossible spike.
red_flags: A steady ramp in lockstep with the player; level scaling that removes the reason to get ahead.

lens: What named problem, platform strength or market gap does our concept answer?
look_for: A one-sentence problem statement and a core rule that changes what the player does; a design element that only this platform can deliver.
red_flags: Novelty that renames the usual verb; a concept that would be the same on any platform; a crowded genre chosen from trend data.

lens: Can a novice finish with only the core, and does the optional depth reward veterans?
look_for: A playthrough with only the basic verbs reaches the end; depth systems and extras sit where players choose them; the harshest penalty suits the target player.
red_flags: Progress gated by the depth system; extras forced on everyone; risk tuned to the team's skill.

lens: Given our team, tools and remaining time, is this a concept we can finish, and what does our situation make uniquely possible?
look_for: Dev time estimated for each candidate; carried-over team, tools and assets listed; the plan uses that head start boldly.
red_flags: A concept chosen without a time estimate; a one-time opportunity left unused.

lens: Do our characters, stages or vehicles change the rules, or only the art?
look_for: Each variant is a parameter set that changes how it plays and sounds; players can name favorites and say why.
red_flags: Reskins with barely different stats; separate code per variant.

lens: Has the final balance been checked on production hardware after the last optimization?
look_for: Processing speed and timing locked before tuning; difficulty and timers replayed on retail units; a narrow fix ready if launch reveals a problem.
red_flags: Tuning only on dev boards; optimizations after balance sign-off; game speed tied to processing speed.

lens: Before cutting a feature or content, have we tried changing its context or using the limit as a design idea?
look_for: Screen space, arena bounds, speed, camera and roles tried as levers; memory and screen limits answered with reuse, authored patterns or bigger targets.
red_flags: Signature mechanics cut at the first balance problem; limits treated only as subtraction.

lens: For a sequel, what is the one-line headline, and does every element have an upgrade target?
look_for: A headline tied to new hardware, audience or team continuity; an element-by-element upgrade list.
red_flags: 'More of the same' at the same scale.

lens: If players or partners don't get the game, where can they learn why it is deep?
look_for: A players' guide or regular explanation in the words of whoever knows the game best.
red_flags: Waiting for the press to explain a new concept.

lens: Would a player accept every compromise in this build?
look_for: Each shortcut is either invisible to players or was chosen after alternatives were tried with programmers; the team can say how each decision entertains the player.
red_flags: Specs justified by 'it was easier to build'; known flaws waved through because the schedule was hard; 'players won't notice' said about things they will.

lens: Is this pace one you could keep for years?
look_for: Short self-imposed deadlines, small recurring outputs, reviews cleared daily, a protected work block, exercise and a sane screen setup.
red_flags: Reviews piling up overnight, late-night deliveries, all-or-nothing crunches, routine work done out of obligation, nobody exercising.

lens: What have you played and learned from lately?
look_for: The team has finished a range of recent games in and around the genre, has notes on why things worked, and knows the genre's classics.
red_flags: Everyone plays the same one game; references are all from childhood; nobody can name what a competitor does better.

lens: Who is waiting on you right now?
look_for: No review or decision older than a day; one channel for requests; changes explained to everyone involved.
red_flags: Teammates blocked on your reply; decisions deferred while you deliberate; feedback given to one person and relayed.

lens: What in this game could only have come from you?
look_for: Mechanics rebuilt from an understanding of why they work, a personal take on major decisions, and reasons a player would pick it over the game that inspired it.
red_flags: Features copied without knowing why they work; a pitch that's 'X but with Y'; nothing the team can name as distinctive.

lens: Are you hearing real disagreement, and still protecting what's distinctive?
look_for: Feedback sought from outside the usual circle, sorted into problems to fix and pressure to resist; decisions made by the person with the big picture, with reasons.
red_flags: Only praise reaching the team; decisions by vote; distinctive choices softened after loud reactions.

lens: Can you state the concept in one line, and is today's work heading toward it?
look_for: A one-line concept everyone can repeat; emergent fun amplified when it serves the concept; proposals that commit to one spec.
red_flags: Mid-project direction changes; scrapped months of work; documents full of 'or we could do this'.

lens: Would you be glad to work with every teammate again?
look_for: Problems raised directly with proposed fixes; no badmouthing; people leave on good terms with work handed off.
red_flags: Grudges, gossip, abandoned tasks, people who feel forced into their jobs.

lens: What did you actually finish this week?
look_for: Steady output: drafts written in one push, a recurring habit kept, a small game or feature finished and shown to someone.
red_flags: Waiting for motivation, endless planning, ideas talked about but never written.

lens: At the moment the player can score, how exposed are they?
look_for: The scoring position is also a dangerous position; rewards carry new risk.
red_flags: Safe spots where the player can still win; screen-clearing options with no cost.
keywords: risk reward proximity exposure scoring position

lens: What does each verb cost the player when they use it?
look_for: Every action has a matching danger: recovery, ammo, stamina, exposure, falling.
red_flags: An action whose benefit has no downside; flight or speed with nothing to oppose it.
keywords: downside opposing force cost verb audit

lens: Is the riskiest option also the most rewarding one?
look_for: Payoff climbs with startup, exposure, wager or accumulated danger.
red_flags: The safe play scores best; the heavy variant is underpaid.

lens: Where are the stress, relief, growth and progress in this section?
look_for: A clear squeeze, a satisfying release, a reward that strengthens the player, and a next goal.
red_flags: No obstacle at all, or a release that leads nowhere.

lens: Can you state in one sentence why this mechanic is fun?
look_for: A risk-and-reward explanation that would survive changing the surface action.
red_flags: 'Because game X does it'; an idea that only renames the genre's default action.

lens: What decision does each rule create for the players?
look_for: Every mechanic adds a read, a counter or a trade-off; reads can beat raw stats.
red_flags: Inherited rules with no decision attached; outcomes settled by the first hit or the bigger number.

lens: What does the player get, what can they do with it, and when?
look_for: Rewards planned early, earned through play, spent on things that help with the next challenge.
red_flags: Currency with nothing worth buying; everything unlocked at the start; rewards that snowball.

lens: After a loss, does the player want one more try?
look_for: Short restarts, an entertaining defeat, 'I'll get you next time!'.
red_flags: Long waits after death; defeat that only humiliates.

lens: What is this game's main source of fun, and is the polish budget going there?
look_for: A named source (essence, control feel, story, fandom, simulation, creation, rhythm) with matching investment, and risk layered in where it fits.
red_flags: Assuming story alone carries the game; essence pushed so hard the game loses flair or becomes a chore.

lens: From each press to the first visible or audible response, how many frames pass, and does every press in every state get a reaction?
look_for: The pose changes on the first frame after input; every accepted press has a distinct cue; display and audio lag have been checked on the actual setup.
red_flags: Easing out of idle before the windup; dead buttons in menus or cutscenes; testers saying the controls feel 'floaty' or 'heavy' on one screen but not another.
keywords: responsiveness input lag first frame feedback

lens: When a hit lands, a boss falls or the player dies, does the game stop and shake enough to feel the weight and see what happened?
look_for: Hit stop scaled by strength, victim shaking more than attacker, boss stops with a flash, deaths with a visible point of impact, shake presets matched to impact size.
red_flags: 'Wait, I got hit?'; every hit feeling the same; shake so strong the screen is unreadable.
keywords: impact hitstop screen shake big moments

lens: Does every attack that looks like it connects actually connect, at every damage level, from every direction?
look_for: Hitboxes a little wider than the weapon in fast games, ranges crossing the median line, multi-hit strings that always connect, collision and animation that agree.
red_flags: Visible hits that whiff; hits after the swing ends; combos that drop at some damage percentages; complaints about hits 'not registering'.

lens: How many seconds per session is the player not in control, and how long from failure to the next attempt?
look_for: Hasty transitions that still read as transitions, loading hidden in-world or shown at once, failure effects of about a second, skippable and pausable cutscenes.
red_flags: Slow fades, long black screens, waits that look like mistakes, long death sequences, respawning into danger.

lens: Can you state each action's startup, hit and recovery in frames, and does the build match by feel?
look_for: Specs written in frames; hits about 1/4 to 1/3 in; strong moves with long recoveries; cancel frames where players expect control; a stable target frame rate.
red_flags: Timing described in words; strong attacks that are safe; control returning only at standby; frame drops during the heaviest scenes.
keywords: frames timing recovery cancel frames frame rate

lens: Does each character's movement, jump and knockback feel like its intended weight and serve the game's goal?
look_for: Distinct weights with identical inputs, a jump shaped for its purpose, knockback that always produces a visible reaction, values retuned after every tempo change.
red_flags: Every character feeling the same; a default jump; launches too fast to follow; parameters carried over from another game.

lens: Does the camera show the motion the player just made and the space they need?
look_for: Characters rising on screen when they jump, drifting off center on dodges, look-ahead in scrollers, enough screen for play, comfort toggles for inertial effects.
red_flags: A center point locked to the character; jumps whose height can't be judged; tiny targets; motion-sick testers with no options.
keywords: camera framing screen space motion sickness

lens: Could a genre newcomer pick up the controls in minutes, and can every player change them?
look_for: Direction-plus-button controls, analog tilt and flick used physically, standard layouts, remapping with profiles, adjustable sensitivity.
red_flags: Command strings for basic moves, two-step dashes, inputs added because the hardware has them, no remapping.

lens: Would a stranger know what kind of game this is within the first seconds of the trailer?
look_for: Gameplay or a clear demonstration of the systems right away, the game's appeal up front, story and world later.
red_flags: Logos and opening movies first; no gameplay on the store page; a teaser-only reveal for a new IP.

lens: Does every piece of marketing match how the game actually plays?
look_for: Title, cover, banner, screenshots, trailer and demo all set expectations the game meets; any surprise still fits the overall picture.
red_flags: Art or footage that promises a different genre or mood; a demo that is unbalanced or unrepresentative.

lens: Who is this for, and what else competes for their time?
look_for: A target described by experience and need, chosen from a view of the market; a list of old, new and non-game competitors with a reason to choose this game.
red_flags: 'It's for everyone', or 'for people like me'; a concept picked because data says the genre sells; selling on hour counts.

lens: Does the dev team own a plan to make this game known?
look_for: Reveal assets, site, demo decisions and update cadence in the schedule; the director reviewing official posts; assets made for reuse.
red_flags: Marketing left until the end; 'a good game sells itself'; no one from development reviewing what goes out.

lens: Would you ship this build if no patch were ever possible?
look_for: Release quality judged as final; post-launch work triaged into fatal fixes and optional bonuses; contained fixes preferred.
red_flags: 'We'll patch it later'; core systems rewritten in hotfixes; DLC scheduled as if it were free.

lens: When people misunderstand the game, where do they get the designer's explanation?
look_for: A guide or regular posts in the director's words explaining the essence and push and pull, on a home base players can find.
red_flags: Depending entirely on press and social chatter to explain an unusual game.

lens: Is every showcase shot as bold as it can be?
look_for: Tight, confident framing, interactions between characters, a mix of serious and comic beats, cuts on the music, no needless blur.
red_flags: Safe medium shots, focus pulls, footage captured live when replay tools could have found a better angle.

lens: How do fans' voices reach the team, and how are they filtered?
look_for: Structured input at planning time, recurring requests answered, a clear line between what is open to input and what is fixed.
red_flags: Plans swinging with each comment thread; persistent requests ignored; reading only the loudest agreeing voices.

lens: Within three minutes of first boot, is the player in control and has the core fun shown itself?
look_for: A newcomer acts within moments, meets a climactic or meaningful situation, and can say what the game is about after three minutes; controls arrive in stages.
red_flags: Logos and lore before the first input; a detached tutorial room; the full control set demanded at once.
keywords: opening onboarding first three minutes tutorial

lens: What share of a session is the player in control, and what is the longest stretch without it?
look_for: Most of the session is in control; transitions are brisk; retries return control in about a second plus load; every non-interactive moment can be skipped or paused.
red_flags: Slow fades and black screens, long death sequences, unskippable scenes, trips back to town after an objective.
keywords: player time downtime pacing control time

lens: Can the concept be stated in one sentence, and does every task in progress serve it?
look_for: One clear statement of appeal, naming the audience or hook; current work traces back to it; emergent fun is amplified in the same direction.
red_flags: Several competing visions; direction changes because development feels hard; nobody can say who the game is for.

lens: Has the core fun been played in a build, before content production began?
look_for: A bare prototype or finished-quality pilot exists and convinced people; open questions in the spec are tied to builds that will answer them.
red_flags: Months of content on top of an unproven core; a spec that pretends to know everything.

lens: At any moment, what is the player working toward, and can they see how far they have left?
look_for: A visible next reward or objective, progress shown as current versus required, peaks that pay off, rewards that suit the concept.
red_flags: Hidden progress, rewards bolted on late, a steady incline with no peaks or flats, stat growth that breaks a fixed-baseline game.

lens: If the schedule halved tomorrow, what goes, what stays locked, and what hidden costs are we carrying?
look_for: A ranked feature list with must-ship items protected, known test and maintenance costs per feature, every hard limit checked.
red_flags: Must-haves like the tutorial left to the end; growth systems added late with no test budget; guideline conflicts found after building.

lens: Could a teammate implement and tune this spec without asking you a question?
look_for: Bracketed plain-language parameters with units, timings in frames, a single committed option, an outline that mirrors the game.
red_flags: Terse or unitless values, 'or we could do this' alternatives, walls of flat text.

lens: Does any cutscene or story beat delay play, undo the player's win, or serve as the reward?
look_for: Story told from the protagonist's view and largely during play; cutscenes short and purposeful; showcase movies treated as marketing.
red_flags: A loss in a cutscene after a player victory; long exposition before control; movies locked behind progress.

lens: Described without naming another game, what does ours offer that players can't get elsewhere?
look_for: Several distinct kinds of appeal, inherited givens questioned, characters and options with one-word identities, a sequel that is clearly bigger.
red_flags: 'X, but with Y'; one small point of difference; characters that are basically the same.

lens: For each open design question, who decides, and does everyone know it?
look_for: One named director (or a written split of who decides what); the decider explains reasons; polls used only as input.
red_flags: Votes on design; two leads each assuming the other will decide; decisions by whoever argues longest.
keywords: director final say decision owner authority vote

lens: How long does a problem take to go from noticed, to raised, to decided?
look_for: Problems raised the same day with facts and a proposed fix; decisions before the meeting ends; research started at once when facts are missing.
red_flags: "I knew that was wrong" in retrospectives; people stuck for days; meetings ending with "we'll decide later".
keywords: escalation latency decision speed blockers raise problems early

lens: Can every teammate state the concept in one sentence and their task's role in it?
look_for: Matching one-sentence answers; changes that tune how the game delivers its appeal rather than replacing the appeal; wrong calls corrected quickly.
red_flags: Different answers from different people; direction changing with each review; a known-bad decision kept because it was already made.
keywords: concept alignment shared goal vision course correction

lens: Is our feedback shown, specific and heard by everyone it affects?
look_for: Retouches or sketches beside the original; notes that name the axis, frame or reference; whole-discipline review sessions; changes explained to everyone involved.
red_flags: Vague notes like "make it look better"; onomatopoeia-only sound notes; feedback relayed through one person; the same note coming back reversed.
keywords: feedback quality visual feedback specific notes group review

lens: What is the oldest unanswered review request or pending decision?
look_for: Nothing older than a working day; a single review channel; a delivery cutoff; the reviewer has a protected block for their own work.
red_flags: Requests piling up overnight; reviews starting late at night; the whole team waiting on one inbox.
keywords: review turnaround approvals bottleneck same day

lens: Could a new teammate build this spec without asking a question?
look_for: Frame counts, units and bracketed parameters; posed-figure or reference images; each asset's gameplay role stated; one committed option instead of A-or-B.
red_flags: Words like "fast"; unlabeled numbers; Plan B left open; convenience choices that players will feel.
keywords: spec quality design document handoff clarity

lens: When did someone new to the game last play it from the start while we watched silently?
look_for: Fresh testers each used once; children or outsiders observed, not interviewed; testers who get motion sick checking the camera; reactions shared with the team.
red_flags: Only the dev team has played; the same outsider reused; asking testers what they think instead of watching.
keywords: playtesting outsiders fresh eyes observation children

lens: Is the director spending time where only the director can help?
look_for: Specialists and testers trusted with execution and analysis; the director supervising, playing the build, cutting scope and stepping into anything stalled.
red_flags: The director doing data entry; a core system still broken after long delegation; cuts left to producer-versus-director fights.

lens: Are we keeping what makes the game and its characters distinctive?
look_for: Weaknesses amplified to offset strengths; director interventions aimed at individuality; deliberate quirks kept despite outside pressure.
red_flags: Every character converging on average; balance changes that only cut strengths; design swayed by whichever opinions agree with us.
keywords: individuality uniqueness balance homogenization echo chamber

lens: Does the team see the whole game and feel heard and respected?
look_for: A daily report people actually read; regular showcases; an answered opinion board; polite requests instead of orders; calm, blame-free problem reviews.
red_flags: People who only see their own slice; important news only in email; orders barked; failures pinned on one person.
keywords: team health information sharing respect morale communication

lens: How long does one tuning change take to reach a playable build, and who can make it?
look_for: Values in an external table; one-press conversion to all dev kits; plain-language names with units; several planners able to tune.
red_flags: Numbers in code; minutes-long conversions or reboots; only the director or one programmer can change values; unitless or cryptic parameters.

lens: Does the game run at the same speed and difficulty on every machine, frame rate and region?
look_for: Logic independent of draw rate and CPU speed; final-build checks on retail hardware; per-controller calibration.
red_flags: Difficulty that changed after optimization; timers tuned only on a dev board; PAL-style speed differences.
keywords: frame rate independence hardware differences timing

lens: Does the heaviest scene hold the frame-rate target on the weakest platform?
look_for: A target set at the start; profiling at maximum load; detail spent where players look; features cut to protect the rate.
red_flags: Budgets set from typical scenes; late drops to 30 fps; detail in places nobody sees.

lens: Was the feel of this build judged on a lag-free setup?
look_for: A jump test on every display before sessions; Game Mode on; audio checked separately.
red_flags: Feel complaints that disappear on another TV; demos on untested displays; picture processing left on.
keywords: input lag display latency playtest setup

lens: Can the team set up any test in seconds and see exactly what they are checking?
look_for: Debug commands for common setups on the normal controller; transparency and per-element toggles; collision and slow-motion views; replay with a free camera.
red_flags: Workarounds such as editing a move's damage to set up a test; separate debug controllers; bloated debug menus; editing models to inspect animation.

lens: Where do systems fight over control in this build, and were those tested first?
look_for: A test matrix estimate; hot-spot list (grabs, scene changes, extreme terrain, growth systems, AI mode conflicts); overnight automated play.
red_flags: Random free-play testing; no prioritization; a bug-free promise.

lens: Is every bug a ticket with repro steps, a class, an owner and a verified fix?
look_for: Latest daily build; S and A classes; routing by discipline; verification in several configurations; resolved tickets kept; regression before patches.
red_flags: Bugs reported in chat; old-build reports; deleted tickets; hotfixes shipped without re-checks.

lens: If no patch ever shipped, would this build be acceptable on day one?
look_for: Content locked early; time spent on near-final builds; a triage plan for crashes versus optional updates; a demo with no leftover spoilers.
red_flags: Known issues deferred to a day-one patch; updates assumed to be free; demo built as a quick slice.

lens: Could a newcomer find, read and safely edit any file in the project?
look_for: Sort-friendly English names; one ID scheme; files on a server with locking, merging and history.
red_flags: Cryptic or romanized names; copies passed by hand; lost edits nobody can recover.

lens: If a player wants the fun right now, how many presses and seconds stand in the way?
look_for: Mashing confirm reaches the main mode; every logo, movie and cutscene skips in one press; text completes on a press; transitions are short.
red_flags: Unskippable logos; skip locked until a scene is watched; slow text crawl; long fades into black screens; stick-tapping through menus.
keywords: player time skip speed menus quick start

lens: Does every button press, in every state, get a clear answer?
look_for: Confirm works on several buttons; presses in cutscenes bring up a skip prompt; each accepted press has a sound or highlight.
red_flags: Dead buttons; presses with ambiguous or no feedback; cutscenes that ignore input.

lens: Could someone who cannot read the language still use this screen?
look_for: Pictures on major icons; a color per section; important options largest; help text in plain words for those who can read.
red_flags: Text-only menus; help text that repeats item names; jargon; equal-weight lists of many options.
keywords: wordless clarity icons color help text

lens: Can each player set up controls and comfort the way they need, without restarting?
look_for: In-game remapping with profiles and safe assignment; accessibility menu with presets; previews; difficulty changeable at any time.
red_flags: Fixed controls; actions that can end up unbound; assists toggled by accident; camera comfort signed off by a team that never gets sick.

lens: Where are the player's eyes during play, and is the information there?
look_for: Navigation on the main screen; HUD elements that hide or fade when not needed; essentials away from cropped edges.
red_flags: Players staring at the mini-map; markers always visible; HUD covering characters.

lens: Is every word readable on the real display, in every language?
look_for: Text checked on the smallest target screen per language; room for long strings; font-size option; translators control emphasis.
red_flags: English-only layouts; text approved only on a big dev monitor; labels that overflow icon tiles in translation.

lens: Does this menu belong to this game's world while staying clear?
look_for: A deliberate place between clarity and style; themed fonts, frames, icons and loading indicator; one dominant color per screen; sensible drawer-like grouping.
red_flags: Default fonts; generic Now Loading text; a jumble of colors; flat lists for huge feature sets; style that hides meaning.
keywords: UI style worldbuilding fonts menu organization

lens: Can the player see what a choice will do and where they stand?
look_for: Visual previews of parts and settings; current-versus-required progress on screen; scores in a meaningful unit; ranks that rise with improvement; fast sorting and auto-equip.
red_flags: Stats shown only as numbers; hidden progress; raw leaderboard positions; look-alike item icons.
keywords: preview progress score rank inventory customization

lens: Freeze the busiest frame: can a newcomer tell where the ground is, who is who, what just hit and what's dangerous?
look_for: Terrain, characters, platforms and projectiles are the most prominent things; characters stay visible inside effects; threats have visual tells.
red_flags: Backdrop outshining terrain; fighters lost in shadow, stained glass or layered effects; projectiles lost against a contrasty floor.

lens: Filled in solid black, is every character exaggerated, readable and distinct from the rest of the cast?
look_for: Exaggerated signature features, clear limbs in key poses from the main view, bright extremities.
red_flags: Similar outlines, realistic proportions that blur together, symmetric front-facing poses.

lens: Through a color-blindness filter and in grayscale, does everything that matters still separate?
look_for: Gameplay-critical colors differ in brightness; background darker or calmer than foreground in value.
red_flags: Pieces or pickups that merge; backgrounds brighter than the foreground; a mishmash of colors.

lens: On the brightest and darkest backgrounds, does every effect and flash still pop?
look_for: Crisp focal shapes, dark accents in bright effects, hit flashes with internal contrast.
red_flags: All-additive effects that wash out; white flashes that make characters vanish.

lens: Is each effect as big, as long and as placed as the event it marks?
look_for: Hit marks at the contact point, sized to strength, short for rapid hits; explosions with flash, blast, smoke and a natural end, hitbox shorter than the visual.
red_flags: Generic sparks, floating marks, lingering clutter, explosions cut short or made of one sprite.

lens: In the final frame at gameplay distance, does the scene have believable light and scale?
look_for: Visible light direction and color, saturation falling with distance, large objects that don't look like toys, flames with density.
red_flags: Flat base colors, oversaturated glossy giants, candle-like flames, art approved only in a model viewer.

lens: Is the detail where players actually look, and are targets big enough on the real screen?
look_for: Detail in front of the camera and on playable surfaces; enemies and bosses sized for the screen and audience.
red_flags: Effort spent on unseen details; tiny targets on a handheld; models over-budgeted for their screen size.

lens: Do all characters and assets look like one game, and do adapted ones feel like their originals?
look_for: A shared visual concept from image boards; mixed styles met in the middle; adaptations checked side by side with the source.
red_flags: A fight between live action and animation; literal copies that feel wrong; changes that betray what fans love.

lens: Does each character's look and effects tell the player what it is and what its moves do best?
look_for: Weapon-specific trails, status shown on the body, poses and faces exaggerated enough to read at game size.
red_flags: Shared generic effects, subtle expressions on small characters, inherited realism nobody questioned.

lens: After an hour of play, is anything glaring, strobing, blurry or nauseating, and can players turn it down?
look_for: Capped glow brightness, brief and mild flashing scaled by camera distance, subtle blur with an option, no gratuitous depth of field.
red_flags: Searing magma, full-screen strobes up close, fuzzy motion blur, focus pulls in gameplay.
